headline: Somatic variant calling is shifting onto pangenome and germline-composite references
label: Pangenome Somatic Variant Discovery
summary: A benchmark shows pangenomes improve somatic calling over GRCh38, and two preprints apply germline-aware references to long-read somatic SV discovery.
synthesis: The common thread is anchoring somatic analysis to germline-informed references rather than GRCh38. A published benchmark reports that graph and personalized pangenomes improve somatic variant calling accuracy relative to GRCh38. Two preprints extend this to somatic structural variants from long reads: JANUS discovers them directly in tumor-normal pangenome graphs from HiFi reads without prior alignment, and VESPA-SS uses tumor-specific strings computed against a draft composite germline reference. The new element is treating the germline-aware graph or composite reference as the primary frame for somatic discovery, including alignment-free formulations. GraffiTE, a Nextflow pipeline for genotyping structural variants and annotating polymorphic transposable elements, is only loosely related, as its summary does not describe somatic calling.
